title: SonicRoute
tagline: Send each app's audio to the device you choose.
intro: Keep music on your speakers and games or calls on your headset. SonicRoute is a Windows audio utility that lives in the system tray: choose output and input devices for individual apps, control audio with hotkeys, the tray wheel or a panel, and combine routine actions into automation rules.

steps: Start SonicRoute, find its icon in the Windows notification area (it may be under hidden icons), and double-click it to open the full interface.
Select your preferred output and input devices in Settings.
Click the tray icon to open a panel, or set up your hotkeys. Create automation rules when you want to combine actions.
commandNote: `sr` connects only to an already-running SonicRoute instance; it does not start the app. Before first use, start SonicRoute normally to register the command, then close and reopen your terminal. See the {faq} if device switching does not work as expected.

releaseSummary: Version {version} adds direct default-output selection from the tray, controls for the pinned current app’s volume, mute and routing, mute-all-microphones control, and a tray-wheel pause setting saved across restarts. The default hotkey for system-default volume is Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Wheel, distinct from the default Ctrl+Alt+Wheel hotkey for the current app. Settings toggles have been rearranged and pages now load on demand. featuresCore: **Route audio for individual apps.** Choose each app's playback and recording devices, switch devices for running apps, or change the Windows defaults. Windows keeps app routing settings after SonicRoute exits.

**Control the app you're using.** Recent mode follows the foreground app when it has an audio session. You can also choose the app you last acted on or a specified app. Filter and rename your preferred devices, then cycle through them with the same hotkey.

**Hotkeys and the tray wheel.** Bind keyboard combinations, mouse side buttons and wheel combinations. Scroll over the taskbar's notification area to adjust the current app's volume, and assign a separate shortcut to mute every microphone. The tray menu can directly select the default output device, and control the fixed current app’s volume, mute state and routing. Pause tray-wheel volume changes from the tray menu; this choice is saved across restarts.

**Two panels with different roles.** The Quick panel manages apps in individual rows and controls the selected output device at the top; the App panel focuses on the current app. OSD feedback, app audio meters and microphone mute indicators make the state easy to see.
featuresMore: **One trigger, multiple actions.** {triggerCount} triggers and {actionCount} actions cover device switching, volume, mute, program launches, PowerShell and OSD. Add a delay or stop-on-failure setting to each step, or call another rule. `{ruleCommand}` submits a rule only to an already-running SonicRoute instance; before first use, start SonicRoute normally to register the command, then reopen your terminal.
**Make it your own.** Adjust light/dark themes, accent colors, opacity and panel position. Nine built-in languages support JSON import and export.
